claim.pdf_says:
Adlam:
1E900-1E943, 1E94B

[end of page 980] ... [top of page 981]

Ahom:
11700-1171A
claim.why_it_matters: The script-name label 'Ahom:' that heads page 981 has been appended to the last data line of page 980, so the Adlam range line now reads as though it ended with the token 'Ahom:' and the Ahom range 11700-1171A is left with no label at the top of the next page. Annex B is normative; any reader or tool that pairs a script name with the code ranges beneath it mis-associates two consecutive scripts at this boundary.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed by rendering both PDF pages at 300 dpi and cropping the boundary regions to inspect the printed glyphs directly. PDF page 1010 (printed folio 980) ends its body text with exactly two lines, 'Adlam:' then '1E900-1E943, 1E94B', followed by whitespace and the footer '980  (C)ISO/IEC 2023'. No token 'Ahom' appears anywhere on that page. PDF page 1011 (printed folio 981) begins its body with 'Ahom:' on its own line, then '11700-1171A', then a blank line and 'Anatolian_Hieroglyphs:'. The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 40182 reads '1E900-1E943, 1E94B Ahom:' and the page-1011 body then opens with the bare range '11700-1171A' at line 40188. Both sources are quoted accurately by the claim. This is not page-break furniture, line wrapping, or hyphenation: no header, footer, or folio is involved, and nothing was re-wrapped within a paragraph. A discrete content token, the normative script-name label 'Ahom:', was pulled backwards across the page boundary and concatenated onto a different entry's data line. The meaning does change at the structural level that this list encodes. Annex B.3 is a strict label/ranges list where each 'Script_Name:' line owns the code ranges on the line beneath it, and that pairing is the entire semantic content of the annex. As transcribed, Adlam's range list terminates in the non-hexadecimal token 'Ahom:', and the range 11700-1171A is orphaned with no owning script. A consumer building the XID_Start table for the user-defined-word lexer from this markdown would either fail to parse 'Ahom:' as a range or silently mis-attribute it. The union of code points happens to survive intact, which is why this is structural rather than content-loss, matching the claimed severity. The defect is also not isolated: the same backwards-pull occurs at every Annex B page boundary. A scan for range lines terminating in an appended label ('^[0-9A-F][0-9A-F, -]+ [A-Za-z_]+:$') returns 19 hits across both repertoire lists, at lines 40182, 40235, 40403, 40454, 40506, 40558, 40610, 40772, 40824, 40876, 40928, 40981 (the XID_Start list in B.3 paragraph 1) and 49030, 49087, 49207, 49263, 49319, 49374, 49431 (the later XID_Continue list). The instance immediately following this one is corroborated by the same renders: page 1011 ends with 'Buginese:' / '1A00-1A16' and the markdown line 40235 reads '1A00-1A16 Buhid:'. The claim is therefore accurate as written for page 1010, and understates the scope.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed as described for page 1010, with the scope broadened. The normative Annex B script label 'Ahom:', which is the first body line of PDF page 1011 (printed folio 981), has been appended to the final data line of page 1010 (printed folio 980), producing '1E900-1E943, 1E94B Ahom:' at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 40182 and leaving the Ahom range '11700-1171A' label-less at line 40188. No code range is lost; the damage is to the label/ranges pairing that carries the annex's meaning, so a tool ingesting B.3 to build the user-defined-word character table would choke on 'Ahom:' as a range token or mis-attribute the orphaned range. This is a systematic page-boundary transcription defect rather than a one-off: 19 Annex B page boundaries exhibit the identical backwards-pull of the next page's script label onto the previous page's last range line, at markdown lines 40182, 40235, 40403, 40454, 40506, 40558, 40610, 40772, 40824, 40876, 40928, 40981, 49030, 49087, 49207, 49263, 49319, 49374 and 49431. A fix should repair all 19 uniformly rather than patching this boundary alone.
